behavior: When the item that has the tab stop of a composite becomes disabled while the focus is outside the composite, and the arrow keys skip that item, the tab stop moves to the active item when the arrow keys reach it, or else to the first item that they reach. When the item becomes disabled while it has the focus, the tab stop moves when the focus leaves. At the mount, a checked radio that is a disabled native button also gives the tab stop to the first radio that the arrow keys reach. The arrow keys skip a natively disabled item. They also skip an `aria-disabled` item, unless the root gives `disabledIndices` and the item is not in it. Thus the Tab key does not focus a radio that the arrow keys skip in a Radio Group with no checked radio, and a Toggle Group or a Menubar stays in the order of the Tab key. `Toolbar.Root` keeps the tab stop on a disabled item that stays focusable. An active item that becomes disabled keeps the tab stop while it can get focus, as at the mount. In Base UI, an item that becomes disabled keeps the tab stop, and at the mount a checked radio keeps it also when it is a disabled native button. The Tab key then focuses a disabled radio, or it skips a whole Radio Group, Toggle Group or Menubar, because the item with the tab stop has the `disabled` attribute. A native control also follows its fieldset when it or its wrapper moves. Controls in the first legend keep the native exemption.
